---
id: SA-0256
title: tests/test_draft.py restates saffron/draft.py's own route-to-state table, so a change to one escapes the other
type: bug
priority: 3
estimated_lines: 42
estimate_measured: true
touches:
  - tests/test_draft.py
forbidden:
  - DESIGN.md
  - CONTEXT.md
  - CLAUDE.md
  - README.md
  - pyproject.toml
  - uv.lock
  - .saffron/**
  - .claude/**
  - ontology/**
  - tests/ontology/**
  - docs/**
  - images/**
  - harness/**
  - records/**
  - hooks/**
  - saffron/**
  - tests/test_batch.py
  - tests/test_cli.py
  - tests/test_finish.py
  - tests/test_ledger.py
  - tests/test_ledger_fold_task.py
  - tests/test_package.py
  - tests/test_qualify.py
  - tests/test_reconcile.py
  - tests/test_report.py
  - tests/test_session.py
  - tests/test_suite.py
  - tests/test_worktree.py
budget_usd: 10
max_attempts: 3
max_turns: 30
acceptance:
  - claim: >-
      `_expect` in `tests/test_draft.py` takes the task's route-to-state
      table through a `route_state` parameter. `_run` fills it from
      `saffron.draft._ROUTE_STATE` itself, with a local import beside
      `_slug_for_text`'s own. The module keeps no second table of its
      own. Patching `saffron.draft._ROUTE_STATE` moves the task's own end
      state. It moves what `_expect` predicts for it too, for a route
      round 1 reads and one round 2 reads after a revision.
    witness: tests/test_draft.py::test_the_expected_route_state_tracks_saffron_draft_s_own_table
    wrong_versions:
      - "`_expect` keeps its own module-level `_ROUTE_STATE` dict, and never gains a `route_state` parameter."
      - "`_expect` gains `route_state`, but `_run` still hand-builds its own dict rather than importing `saffron.draft._ROUTE_STATE`."
      - Round 1's lookup reads `route_state`, but round 2's still reads a module-level `_ROUTE_STATE` kept for that one call.
      - Round 2's lookup reads `route_state`, but round 1's still reads a module-level `_ROUTE_STATE` kept for that one call.
---

## Context

Backlog item **b-98a3be**, the Standards lens's remit under ADR 8: "Is a
type, constant or helper the repo already defines imported, not restated?"
(`docs/adr/0008-review-reads-each-hunk-against-the-standing-instructions.md:57-58`).
Found by review at `SA-0227`'s own head, `a53f2c51`. Every line number
below was read at `2f68b96c`, this spec's own base.

**The one real table.** `saffron/draft.py:34-40` defines `_ROUTE_STATE`, a
comment and a four-entry dict mapping each `spec_review_route` outcome to
the `DraftState` it ends a task in. `draft_spec`'s own `_end` reads it at
`saffron/draft.py:168`, through the module-level name alone.

**The restated copy.** `tests/test_draft.py:220-226` defines a second
`_ROUTE_STATE`, the same comment and the same four entries, at module scope
in the test file. `_expect` reads it twice, once for the route round 1
picks (`tests/test_draft.py:295`) and once for round 2's
(`tests/test_draft.py:315`). Nothing ties the two dicts together. A change
to one is invisible to whichever test reads the other.

**The established pattern for borrowed helpers.** `_run` already imports
`_slug_for_text` from `saffron.draft` inside its own body
(`tests/test_draft.py:356-368`). It hands that import to `_expect` as the
`slug_for_text` keyword. `_expect`'s own `one_round` helper calls
`saffron.spec_review.read_spec_review` and `spec_review_route` directly.
Both are imported at module scope (`tests/test_draft.py:22-27`). Only
`_declares_other` is kept as an independent reimplementation, by its own
docstring's own account (`tests/test_draft.py:30-38`). It is the one piece
of logic criterion 2 of `SA-0227` tests directly. `_ROUTE_STATE` is a
plain mapping with no logic of its own, so it carries none of that
reasoning.

## Problem

Two copies of the route-to-state table now have to be kept in sync by
hand. A change to either one, a renamed state, a new route, a swapped
value, reaches only the copy it touches. The other test still reads its
own stale entry, and nothing fails to say so.

## Out of scope

- **`saffron/draft.py` itself.** It already imports every name it needs,
  and this spec touches no production code. `saffron/**` is forbidden.
- **The other borrowed names** `_slug_for_text`, `read_spec_review` and
  `spec_review_route` already name. They stay exactly as `SA-0227` left
  them.
- **`_declares_other`'s independent reimplementation.** It is kept apart
  from `saffron.draft._declares_other_id` on purpose, for the reason its
  own docstring gives. This spec does not touch it.

## Notes for the agent

**The change is an edit to code that exists.** `tests/test_draft.py` is
not new at this spec's own base. Even so, no mutant can pin a value this
claim's own fix changes: the table's entries read the same before and
after, since nothing about `saffron/draft.py`'s own `_ROUTE_STATE` moves.
So the claim's witness is new code of its own, a test that perturbs the
shared table by hand, and `witness` reports `skip`. Each wrong version
above is an edit `REVIEW` turns into, and the witness it names must fail
on every one. Do not run them yourself.

**What the witness does.** It is new, and sits in `tests/test_draft.py`
beside the other tests `SA-0227` added, after
`test_each_route_and_each_writer_stop_ends_the_draft_in_its_own_state` and
before `test_each_session_is_one_attempt_and_each_round_records_its_own_findings`.
It imports `saffron.draft` inside its own body, as the module's own
docstring requires. It uses `monkeypatch.setitem` on the live `saffron.draft._ROUTE_STATE`
dict, moving one route's state to a different valid one. Then it runs one
`Case` through `_run`. It checks the returned `Expected`, the `Drafted`
and the ledger's own `state` column all agree on the moved value. One
`Case` ends through round 1's lookup, with no review round that revises.
One ends through round 2's, after a review that routes `revise` and a
second round that escalates. Patching two different routes, one per case,
picks apart a build that fixes one lookup and leaves the other restated.
It still fails, on the case that reaches the one left unfixed.

**Measured on a prototype, 2026-10-09.** On this head, with the fix
applied, all six tests in `tests/test_draft.py` pass, and so does
`tests/test_ledger_fold_task.py`. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check`
both pass on the changed file, and the `prose`, `structure` and `dead`
gates report no new hit there. Each of the four wrong versions above was
applied to the prototype by hand, and the new witness failed on every
one. The diff measured 170 changed tokens against the `bug` ceiling of
1300.
